# Adjudication Task — Chapter 368

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃368화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|소년, 아니 문경이라는 이름을 가진 ‘그’는 발아래를 굽어보았다.
  6|
  7|믿을 수 없다는 듯이 그를 바라보는 무수한 시선들. 그중 낯익은 얼굴이 있었다.
  8|
  9|오래전 단 한 번 마주쳤을 뿐이지만 그를 알아보는 것은 그리 어려운 일이 아니었다.
 10|
 11|“오랜만일세, 화왕.”
 12|
 13|그의 인사에 화왕 적천강의 눈동자가 격동으로 떨렸다.
 14|
 15|“……정말 당신이었다니.”
 16|
 17|천하제일의 살수. 숱한 무인들로부터 지탄과 경멸을 넘어 경외를 불러일으킨 그는 어느 날 홀연히 사라졌고, 두 번 모습을 드러내지 않았다.
 18|
 19|적어도 촌각 전까지는.
 20|
 21|“어째서 당신이 이곳에…….”
 22|
 23|“많은 일이 있었지. 참으로 많은 일이. 그렇지 않으냐?”
 24|
 25|물음이 향한 곳에는 한 노인이 있었다. 형용할 수 없는 눈빛으로 신의, 아니 동봉을 바라보던 그가 입술을 열었다.
 26|
 27|“다행이구나. 늦지 않아서.”
 28|
 29|그의 입술 사이로 흘러나온 목소리가 천지사방에서 울려 퍼졌다.
 30|
 31|육합전성(六合傳聲).
 32|
 33|눈앞에서 펼쳐진 아득한 무학의 경지에 전율이 흐르는 가운데, 늙은 의원은 작게 고개를 가로저었다.
 34|
 35|“늦으셨습니다.”
 36|
 37|안타까움이 담긴 한마디가 이어졌다.
 38|
 39|“지난 세월을 되돌리시기에는 말입니다.”
 40|
 41|“어찌하겠느냐, 이미 엎어진 물을 주워 담기란 어려운 일인 것을.”
 42|
 43|“후회하지 않으십니까.”
 44|
 45|“후회라.”
 46|
 47|제자의 말에 고개를 들어 하늘을 바라보았다.
 48|
 49|영원히 쏟아질 것 같던 빗줄기도, 햇빛을 가리고 있던 먹구름도 사라진 그곳에 푸르른 창천이 펼쳐져 있다.
 50|
 51|‘이것이 당신의 뜻이오?’
 52|
 53|저 위에서 하계(下界)를 내려다보고 있을 누군가에게 던지는 물음.
 54|
 55|그러나 대답은 돌아오지 않는다. 언제나 그래 왔듯이.
 56|
 57|‘참으로…… 빌어먹을 일이로군.’
 58|
 59|그는 지그시 눈을 감았다. 캄캄한 어둠 속에서 피와 투쟁으로 점철된 기억이 스쳐 지나간다.
 60|
 61|살수로 키워져 살수로 살았던 지난 삶. 타고난 업이 살수라 사람을 죽였고, 타고나길 사람이라 살생이 싫었다.
 62|
 63|대륙을 피로 물들인 대전쟁의 끝자락에서, 늙은 살수가 병장기를 파묻고 의원으로 살아간 것은 그런 이유에서였다.
 64|
 65|하지만…….
 66|
 67|끝내 이렇게 되었는가.
 68|
 69|작은 중얼거림과 함께 감았던 눈을 떴다.
 70|
 71|새하얗고 부드러운 소년의 손.
 72|
 73|수년 전 찾아온 반로환동(返老還童)은 피륙을 바꿔 놓았을지언정, 손에 배인 혈향마저 지울 수는 없었다.
 74|
 75|“의원으로 사십여 년을 살았다. 의원으로 죽고자 했다.”
 76|
 77|거대한 공력을 담은 목소리가 천둥이 되어 귓전을 파고든다. 심령(心靈)을 뒤흔들리는 듯한 충격을 받은 흑의인들이 신형을 휘청거렸다.
 78|
 79|“한데, 너희는 어찌하여 이곳에 왔느냐.”
 80|
 81|전신의 털이 곤두서는 듯한 살의. 하늘 위의 존재를 보며 얼어붙어 있던 부단주가 떨리는 목소리로 말했다.
 82|
 83|“그, 그대가 정녕 살성이라 한들, 관여할 일이 아니오.”
 84|
 85|“관여할 일이 아니다?”
 86|
 87|낮게 뇌까린 그가 손에 들고 있던 행낭을 던졌다.
 88|
 89|쿵, 땅에 떨어진 행낭에서 튕겨 나간 무언가가 부단주의 발치에 닿았다.
 90|
 91|“이, 이건.”
 92|
 93|그것은 두 사람의 수급이었다. 부릅뜬 눈동자와 일그러진 표정은 각기 다른 사람임에도 똑 닮아 있었다.
 94|
 95|마치 한날한시에 태어난 쌍둥이처럼.
 96|
 97|부단주의 시선은 그중 하나에 고정되어 있었다.
 98|
 99|“단주!”
100|
101|일괴의 수급을 보고 경악하는 부단주를 향해, 그가 천천히 말문을 열었다.
102|
103|“하나만 묻지. 청성(靑城)에 있던 것이 기련삼괴 중 둘째인가, 아니면 셋째인가?”
104|
105|“……!”
106|
107|부단주는 그제야 깨달았다.
108|
109|왜 청성파에서 아무 소식이 없었는지. 그리고 긴급을 알리는 신호를 보고도 돌아오지 않은 형제들은 어디에 있는지.
110|
111|결국 그에게 남은 길은 하나뿐이었다. 섬광 같은 깨달음과 함께, 공력을 실은 외침이 터져 나왔다.
112|
113|“모두 공격하라! 놈을 죽…….”
114|
115|서걱!
116|
117|부단주의 외침은 이어지지 못했다.
118|
119|목을 스치는 바람과 함께 비틀거리는 그의 뒤에, 어느새 한 사람이 서 있었다.
120|
121|‘이, 이것이 정녕…… 사람의 움직임이란 말인가.’
122|
123|마지막으로 뇌리를 스치는 의문.
124|
125|천하제일, 아니 고금제일의 살수가 펼친 유령환살보(幽靈幻殺步)를 알아보지 못한 그를 기다리는 것은 죽음뿐이었다.
126|
127|푸화아악!
128|
129|잘려 나간 목의 단면에서 피 분수가 솟구쳤다. 무너지는 신형을 스치며 한 사람이 걸음을 내디뎠다. 동시에 혈향을 머금은 바람이 불었다.
130|
131|서걱, 서걱, 서걱!
132|
133|넋 나간 얼굴로 상관의 죽음을 지켜보던 흑의인들의 목이 허공으로 붕 떠올랐다.
134|
135|핏줄기가 땅이 닿기도 전에 유령처럼 희끄무레한 무언가가 그들을 지나쳤다.
136|
137|“그토록 원했던 삶이었건만.”
138|
139|그는 낮게 읊조리며 양손을 뻗었다. 열 개의 손가락에서 가늘고 긴 실이 흘러나온다.
140|
141|아름다우면서도 파괴적인 강기(劍罡)의 실이.
142|
143|“너희는 어찌하여…….”
144|
145|슈와아악!
146|
147|구부려진 열 개의 손가락이 허공을 그어 내리자, 강기가 공간을 찢었다.
148|
149|동시에 막아서는 모든 것이 베이고 갈라졌다. 조각조각 난 갑옷과 병장기, 사지와 목이 사방으로 솟구쳤다.
150|
151|피와 죽음으로 정지한 세상 속에서, 오직 한 사람만이 자유로웠다.
152|
153|“나를 깨웠느냐.”
154|
155|한탄과 분노에 사로잡힌 그는 더 이상 명랑하던 소년도, 제자에게 신의라는 두 글자를 물려준 의원도 아니었다.
156|
157|신의라는 이름을 얻기 전, 역병으로 처자식을 잃어 슬픔에 잠겨 있던 젊은 목수를 만나기 전, 그리고 병장기를 파묻고 무림을 떠나기 전의 그로 돌아가 있었다.
158|
159|“살성(殺星)……!”
160|
161|누군가 내지른 비명 같은 외침.
162|
163|심연보다 깊이 가라앉은 눈빛을 한 그가 양팔을 떨쳤다. 어느덧 폭풍이 된 바람이 백여 명의 흑의인들을 집어삼켰다.
164|
165|콰아아아!
166|
167|
168|
169|* * *
170|
171|
172|
173|사천당문의 동쪽에는 높은 언덕이 있다.
174|
175|당문의 경내를 한눈에 내려다볼 수 있는 그곳에는 작은 망루와 교대로 번을 서는 무인들이 존재했다. 아니, 존재했었다.
176|
177|투둑, 툭.
178|
179|망루에서 떨어진 핏방울이 풀잎을 적셨다. 더러는 언덕을 따라 미끄러져 누군가의 손에 닿기도 했다.
180|
181|자글자글하게 주름진 손등과 오랫동안 익힌 독공(毒功)의 영향으로 녹색을 띤 손톱.
182|
183|손의 주인은 사천당문의 당대 가주인 만독수라(萬毒修羅) 당사독이었다.
184|
185|“쿨럭.”
186|
187|바싹 마른 입술 사이로 핏물이 튀었다. 언제나 서늘하고 힘 있던 눈동자는 금방이라도 꺼질 것처럼 위태로웠다.
188|
189|“이렇게 끝나는가.”
190|
191|당사독은 희미한 목소리로 중얼거렸다.
192|
193|모든 것이 끝을 향해 달려가고 있었다. 자신의 명(命)도. 사천당문의 찬란했던 역사도.
194|
195|“수백 년에 걸쳐 쌓아 올린 본가가…… 하루아침에 무너져 내리는구나.”
196|
197|당사독의 한탄은 공허했다. 그에게는 더 이상의 분노와 슬픔을 느낄 기력조차 남아 있지 않았다.
198|
199|사지가 으스러지고 심각한 내상을 입은 늙은 가주에게 유일하게 허락된 것은, 이름 모를 나무에 기대어 자신의 가문이 멸망하는 광경을 지켜보는 것뿐이었다.
200|
201|
202|
203|‘이것이 자네에게 주는 내 마지막 선물일세.’
204|
205|
206|
207|미소 띤 중년인의 얼굴이 당사독의 눈앞을 스쳤다.
208|
209|중년인, 서천마군은 약속을 지키지 않았다. 그에게 있어 사천당문의 멸문은 처음부터 정해져 있던 것이나 다름없었다.
210|
211|“우웁. 쿠에에엑!”
212|
213|들불처럼 일어난 심화(心火)가 내상을 더욱 악화시킨다. 한 됫박은 될 법한 핏물을 쏟아낸 당사독은 숨을 헐떡였다.
214|
215|“미안하네. 미안해…….”
216|
217|사천당문의 선조들과 못난 가주를 만나 애꿎은 목숨을 잃은 식솔들, 그리고 지금쯤 서천마군에 의해 처참한 죽음을 맞이했을 진태경 일행에게 보내는 사죄였다.
218|
219|물론 그들 중 어느 한 사람도 당사독의 목소리를 들을 수 없을 테지만.
220|
221|‘구천(九泉)에서 만나거든, 내 직접 사죄하겠네.’
222|
223|당사독이 마음속으로 중얼거리던 그때.
224|
225|스스슥.
226|
227|수풀이 들썩이며 가까워지는 인기척이 느껴졌다.
228|
229|아니, 그건 사람의 것이 아니었다. 당사독은 코앞까지 다가온 후에야 이 묘한 기척의 주인공이 누구인지 알 수 있었다.
230|
231|쉬릭, 쉭.
232|
233|날름거리는 혀와 뿔이 달린 세모꼴의 머리. 새하얀 몸통을 지닌 한 마리의 뱀이 당사독의 품을 파고들었다.
234|
235|“허, 허허.”
236|
237|당사독은 기쁘기도 하고 허탈하기도 하여 풀썩 웃어 버렸다.
238|
239|“너였더냐.”
240|
241|취릭.
242|
243|천년독각사, 미미가 주인의 말에 대답하는 것처럼 쉭쉭거렸다. 차가운 혓바닥이 핏물에 엉겨 붙은 수염을 핥는다.
244|
245|“영리한 녀석, 어찌 여기까지 찾아왔을꼬.”
246|
247|당사독은 흐릿한 눈빛으로 자신의 애완뱀을 바라보았다.
248|
249|혹여나 난전(亂戰) 중에 상하지는 않을까 걱정되어 풀어 두었던 녀석이다. 이렇게 다시 만나게 될 것이라고는 생각하지 못했다.
250|
251|그리고…… 이런 식으로 마지막 이별을 하게 될 줄도.
252|
253|구구구궁!
254|
255|거대한 굉음과 함께 진동이 언덕까지 전해진다. 흙이 떠오르고 나무가 가지를 흔들었다.
256|
257|당사독은 고개를 들어 굉음의 진원지를 찾으려 했지만, 이미 흐려진 시각으로는 무슨 일이 벌어지는지 알 수가 없었다.
258|
259|다만 한 가지 사실을 유추할 따름이다.
260|
261|‘때가 되었나.’
262|
263|진천뢰(震天雷)와는 차원이 다른 굉음. 마침내 대 사천당문의 멸망이 코앞까지 들이닥친 것이다.
264|
265|지그시 눈을 감았다 뜬 당사독이 입을 열었다.
266|
267|“떠나거라.”
268|
269|취릭?
270|
271|세모꼴의 주둥이가 갸우뚱 기울어졌다.
272|
273|“노부도, 당문도 얼마 남지 않았다. 이곳에 있으면 너 역시 화를 입게 된다.”
274|
275|당사독은 사천당문의 가주. 서천마군이 아니더라도 누군가는 반드시 찾아와 그의 생사를 확인할 것이다.
276|
277|그때 주인의 곁을 지키는 천년독각사를 본 흉수들이 어찌할지는 능히 짐작하고도 남았다.
278|
279|“그러니 어서 가거라. 어서!”
280|
281|호통이라도 치고 싶건만, 쥐어짜 낸 음성은 금방이라도 끊어질 것처럼 가느다랬다.
282|
283|그러나 당사독과 오랜 세월을 함께한 영물(靈物)은 주인이자 친구였던 그의 마지막 뜻을 알아차렸다.
284|
285|투둑, 툭.
286|
287|당사독의 주름진 손등 위로 축축한 액체가 떨어졌다.
288|

The question was directed at an old man. The man called Mungyeong gazed at the Divine Physician—or rather, Dong Feng—with an indescribable look before speaking.

[P13]
“Thank goodness. I wasn’t too late.”

[P14]
His voice rang out from every direction.

[P15]
Six-Harmonies Voice Transmission.

[P16]
A shudder ran through everyone at the unfathomable realm of martial arts displayed before them. The old physician quietly shook his head.

[P17]
“You were too late.”

[P18]
His next words carried a note of regret.

[P19]
“Too late to turn back the years that have passed.”

[P20]
“What can be done? Once water is spilled, it is not easily gathered again.”

[P21]
“Do you not regret it?”

[P22]
“Regret…”

[P23]
At his Disciple’s words, he raised his head toward the sky.

[P24]
The rain that had seemed as though it would fall forever was gone, as were the dark clouds that had blotted out the sun. All that remained was the vast azure heaven.

[P25]
*Is this what you intended?*

[P26]
He posed the question to someone who might be looking down upon the mortal realm from above.

[P27]
But no answer came.

[P28]
Just as it never had.

[P29]
*What a damned thing this is.*

[P30]
He slowly closed his eyes. In the pitch-black darkness, memories steeped in blood and struggle flashed past.

[P31]
He had been raised as an assassin and lived as one. His inborn karma was that of an assassin, so he killed—but he had been born human, and he hated killing.

[P32]
That was why, near the end of the great war that had stained the continent with blood, the aging assassin had buried his weapons and chosen to live as a physician.

[P33]
But…

[P34]
Had it come to this after all?

[P35]
With a quiet murmur, he opened his eyes.

[P36]
A boy’s hands, pale and soft.

[P37]

[P38]

[P39]

[P40]

“No concern of mine?”

[P45]
Thud!

[P47]
“T-This is…”

[P49]
Like twins born at the same hour on the same day.

[P50]
The deputy captain’s gaze fixed on one of them.

[P51]
“Captain!”

[P52]

[P53]

[P54]
“……!”

[P56]
Why no word had come from the Qingcheng Sect—and where the brothers who had failed to return after seeing the emergency signal had gone.

[P57]

[P58]

[P59]
Slash!

The deputy captain’s shout was cut short.

[P61]

[P62]
*Can this truly be… the movement of a human being?*

[P63]

[P64]
He had failed to recognize the Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step performed by the greatest assassin under heaven—or rather, the greatest assassin in all history.

[P65]
Only death awaited him.

[P66]
Fwoosh!

[P67]

[P68]
Slash. Slash. Slash!

[P69]
The heads of the black-clad men who had watched their superior die in a daze flew into the air.

[P70]

[P71]
“It was the life I wanted so desperately.”

[P72]
Murmuring under his breath, he extended both hands. Long, slender threads streamed from his ten fingers.

[P73]
Beautiful and destructive threads of Sword Force.

[P74]
“And yet, why did you…”

[P75]
Whoosh!

[P76]
His ten curved fingers raked downward through the air, and Sword Force tore through space.

[P77]

In a world brought to a standstill by blood and death, only one person moved freely.

“…wake me?”

[P80]
Consumed by grief and fury, he was no longer the cheerful boy, nor was he the physician who had passed the name Divine Physician down to his Disciple.

[P81]

[P82]
“The Slaughter Saint…!”

[P83]
Someone screamed the name.

[P84]

[P85]
Kwaaang!

* * *

[P87]
A high hill stood east of the Sichuan Tang Clan.

[P88]

[P89]
Once.

[P90]
Drip. Drip.

[P91]

The hand belonged to Tang Sadok, the current Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan—the Myriad-Poison Asura.

[P94]
“Cough.”

[P96]
“Is this how it ends?”

Tang Sadok murmured faintly.

[P98]

[P99]

[P100]

[P101]

[P102]
*This is my final gift to you.*

[P103]
The smiling face of a middle-aged man flashed before Tang Sadok’s eyes.

[P104]
The Western Heaven Demon Lord had not kept his promise. To him, the destruction of the Sichuan Tang Clan had been a foregone conclusion from the very beginning.

[P105]
“Urgh… Blergh!”

[P106]
The rage flaring within him like wildfire worsened his internal injuries. Tang Sadok vomited nearly half a gallon of blood, then gasped for breath.

[P107]
“I’m sorry. I’m sorry…”

[P108]
It was an apology to the ancestors of the Sichuan Tang Clan. To the innocent members of his household who had lost their lives because they had been saddled with an unworthy Family Head. And to Jin Taekyung and his companions, who had likely already met gruesome deaths at the hands of the Western Heaven Demon Lord.

[P109]
Of course, none of them could hear Tang Sadok’s voice.

[P110]
*If we meet in the afterlife, I will apologize to you myself.*

[P111]
Just as Tang Sadok murmured those words inwardly—

[P112]
Rustle.

[P113]
The bushes stirred, and he sensed something approaching.

[P114]
No. It was not human.

[P115]
Only when the strange presence had drawn right up to him did Tang Sadok realize who it belonged to.

[P116]
Hiss. Hiss.

[P117]
A flicking tongue. A horned, triangular head. A pure-white snake burrowed into Tang Sadok’s arms.

[P118]
“Ha… hahaha.”

[P119]
Tang Sadok slumped back with a laugh, both overjoyed and heartsick.

[P120]
“So it was you.”

[P121]
Hisss.

[P122]
The Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, Mimi, hissed as though answering her master. Her cold tongue licked his beard, which was matted with blood.

[P123]
“Clever creature. How did you find me all the way out here?”

[P124]
Tang Sadok gazed at his pet snake through clouded eyes.

[P125]
He had set her loose out of fear that she might be hurt in the chaotic battle. He had never expected them to meet again like this.

[P126]
Nor had he imagined their final farewell would happen this way.

[P127]
Rumble!

[P128]
A tremendous roar sent tremors all the way up the hill. The ground heaved, and the trees shook their branches.

[P129]
Tang Sadok raised his head and tried to find the source, but his failing eyesight could no longer make out what was happening.

[P130]
He could infer only one thing.

[P131]
*Has the time come?*

[P132]
It was a roar on an entirely different scale from Heaven-Shaking Thunder.

[P133]
At last, the destruction of the great Sichuan Tang Clan had reached his doorstep.

[P134]
Tang Sadok slowly closed his eyes, then opened them again.

[P135]
“Leave.”

[P136]
Hiss?

[P137]
The triangular head tilted to one side.

[P138]
“This old man has little time left. Neither does the Tang Clan. If you stay here, you will be caught up in this calamity as well.”

[P139]
Tang Sadok was the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan. Even if the Western Heaven Demon Lord did not come himself, someone would certainly come to confirm whether he was alive or dead.

[P140]
He could easily imagine what the murderers would do if they found the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake guarding her master’s side.

[P141]
“So go. Hurry!”

[P142]
He wanted to roar the words, but the voice he wrung out was so thin it seemed ready to snap.

[P143]
Yet the spiritual creature that had spent so many years beside him understood the final wish of the man who had been both her master and her friend.

[P144]
Drip. Drip.

[P145]
Warm droplets fell onto the back of Tang Sadok’s wrinkled hand.

[P146]
Leaving behind a few tears, Mimi slithered away, her white body gliding across the ground.

[P147]
As her presence receded into the distance, a bitter smile briefly touched Tang Sadok’s lips.

[P148]
“Yes. Go safely.”

[P149]
In his youth, he had roamed the battlefields. After the war, he had devoted his life to helping his father, the Poison King, rebuild the Sichuan Tang Clan.

[P150]
He had always been expected to remain cold and meticulous. He had no friend with whom he could share his heart, no lover, and no child of his own blood.

[P151]
Had that spiritual creature not remained by his side all those years, he could never have endured the loneliness.

[P152]
*From today onward, your name is Mimi. Tang Mimi.*

[P153]
On the day he first encountered the tiny Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, Tang Sadok had given her the Tang family name.

[P154]
They shared neither blood nor even species, but Tang Mimi was a member of the Sichuan Tang Clan, recognized as such by its Family Head.

[P155]
*I have lost everyone, and you alone are the one I send away alive. Hahaha.*

[P156]
Tang Sadok let out a hollow laugh and blinked.

[P157]
Through his fading senses, he heard distant roars and screams rising from below the hill.

[P158]
It must have been the final struggle of those fighting to stave off the clan’s destruction.

[P159]
*This old man is still here! I, Tang Sadok, Family Head of the great Sichuan Tang Clan, am here! Come to me!*

[P160]
The cry, as though wrenched from his throat with blood, never made it past the tip of his tongue.

[P161]
Tang Sadok felt the strength slowly drain from his entire body. His heavy eyelids sank lower, little by little.

[P162]
*I’m tired.*

[P163]
What if he simply closed his eyes and fell into a deep sleep?

[P164]
Perhaps, after a brief nap, he would awaken in the grand armchair in the Family Head’s Hall and find the familiar faces of his household waiting for him.

[P165]
How wonderful it would be if everything that had happened—including his father’s death—were nothing more than a Butterfly Dream.[^1]

[P166]
*Yes. If only it were.*

[P167]
His trembling eyelids slowly sank shut.

[P168]
No—they were just about to close.

[P169]
“Mimi! Quick Attack!”

[P170]
Hisssssss!

[P171]
“……?”

[P172]
*What the hell is this bullshit?*

[P173]
Tang Sadok’s eyes flew open.

[P174]
His vision suddenly cleared, revealing a young man racing toward him and Mimi’s white body shooting through the air like an arrow.

[P175]
“Y-You?”

[P176]
“Wow! A wild Grandpa Tang appeared!”

[P177]
Tang Sadok blinked at Cheongpung, who was grinning brightly despite the blood covering his face.

[P178]
“What… What is going on? How did you…?”

[P179]
Cheongpung answered energetically.

[P180]
“Mimi! Whirlwind!”

[P181]
Whirrrrr!

[P182]
Had Tang Sadok possessed even a shred of strength, he would have cursed them both out.

[P183]
Cheongpung and Mimi realized their mistake too late and bowed their heads.

[P184]
“Ah, I’m sorry.”

[P185]
Hiss.

[P186]
“……”

[P187]
Tang Sadok forgot that he had been half dead only moments ago and stared blankly at the man and snake before him. At last, he managed to speak.

[P188]
“Our family… What happened to our family?”

[P189]
“They all died.”

[P190]
“……!”

[P191]
“Oh. Not the Tang Clan. I meant Dark Heaven’s black-clad men.”

[P192]
*You should have said that first!*

[P193]
As Tang Sadok choked on shock and fury, Cheongpung pressed a finger to his Mingmen acupoint. Warmth like a spring day seeped into his body.

[P194]
“Cheongpung! True Qi Guidance!”

[P195]
*This bastard is going to keep this up until the very end…*

[P196]
Tang Sadok wanted to ask what had happened, but this time he could not resist the drowsiness washing over him.

[P197]
Just before his eyelids closed, a voice as gentle as a spring breeze reached his ears.

[P198]
“It’s all over now. Rest easy.”

[P199]
It was the voice that announced the end of a day longer and darker than any other.

[P200]
[^1]: The Butterfly Dream alludes to the ancient Chinese philosopher Zhuangzi’s dream that he was a butterfly, after which he wondered whether he was a man who had dreamed of being a butterfly or a butterfly dreaming of being a man.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

*This old man is still here! I, Tang Sadok, Family Head of the great Sichuan Tang Clan, am here! Come to me!*

[P160]
The cry, as though wrenched from his throat with blood, never made it past the tip of his tongue.

[P161]
Tang Sadok felt the strength slowly drain from his entire body. His heavy eyelids sank lower, little by little.

[P162]
*I’m tired.*

[P163]
What if he simply closed his eyes and fell into a deep sleep?

[P164]
Perhaps, after a brief nap, he would awaken in the grand armchair in the Family Head’s Hall and find the familiar faces of his household waiting for him.

[P165]
How wonderful it would be if everything that had happened—including his father’s death—were nothing more than a Butterfly Dream.[^1]

[P166]
*Yes. If only it were.*

[P167]
His trembling eyelids slowly sank shut.

[P168]
No—they were just about to close.

[P169]
“Mimi! Quick Attack!”

[P170]
Hisssssss!

[P171]
“……?”

[P172]
*What the hell is this bullshit?*

[P173]
Tang Sadok’s eyes flew open.

[P174]
His vision suddenly cleared, revealing a young man racing toward him and Mimi’s white body shooting through the air like an arrow.

[P175]
“Y-You?”

[P176]
“Wow! A wild Grandpa Tang appeared!”

[P177]
Tang Sadok blinked at Cheongpung, who was grinning brightly despite the blood covering his face.

[P178]
“What… What is going on? How did you…?”

[P179]
Cheongpung answered energetically.

[P180]
“Mimi! Whirlwind!”

[P181]
Whirrrrr!

[P182]
Had Tang Sadok possessed even a shred of strength, he would have cursed them both out.

[P183]
Cheongpung and Mimi realized their mistake too late and bowed their heads.

[P184]
“Ah, I’m sorry.”

[P185]
Hiss.

[P186]
“……”

[P187]
Tang Sadok forgot that he had been half dead only moments ago and stared blankly at the man and snake before him. At last, he managed to speak.

[P188]
“Our family… What happened to our family?”

[P189]
“They all died.”

[P190]
“……!”

[P191]
“Oh. Not the Tang Clan. I meant Dark Heaven’s black-clad men.”

[P192]
*You should have said that first!*

[P193]
As Tang Sadok choked on shock and fury, Cheongpung pressed a finger to his Mingmen acupoint. Warmth like a spring day seeped into his body.

[P194]
“Cheongpung! True Qi Guidance!”

[P195]
*This bastard is going to keep this up until the very end…*

[P196]
Tang Sadok wanted to ask what had happened, but this time he could not resist the drowsiness washing over him.

[P197]
Just before his eyelids closed, a voice as gentle as a spring breeze reached his ears.

[P198]
“It’s all over now. Rest easy.”

[P199]
It was the voice that announced the end of a day longer and darker than any other.

[P200]
[^1]: The Butterfly Dream alludes to the ancient Chinese philosopher Zhuangzi’s dream that he was a butterfly, after which he wondered whether he was a man who had dreamed of being a butterfly or a butterfly dreaming of being a man.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

He had been raised as an assassin and lived as one. His inborn karma was that of an assassin, so he killed—but he had been born human, and he hated killing.

[P32]
That was why, near the end of the great war that had stained the continent with blood, the aging assassin had buried his weapons and chosen to live as a physician.

[P33]
But…

[P34]
Had it come to this after all?

[P35]
With a quiet murmur, he opened his eyes.

[P36]
A boy’s hands, pale and soft.

[P37]
Returned to Youth had transformed his flesh several years ago, but even that could not erase the scent of blood steeped into his hands.

[P38]
“I lived as a physician for more than forty years. I wished to die as one.”

[P39]
His voice, laden with immense internal energy, struck their ears like thunder. The black-clad men staggered as though the sound had shaken their very souls.

[P40]
“And yet, why did you come here?”

[P41]

[P42]

[P43]
“No concern of mine?”

[P44]

[P45]
Thud!

[P46]
Something bounced out of the bag as it struck the ground and rolled to the deputy captain’s feet.

[P47]
“T-This is…”

[P48]

[P49]
Like twins born at the same hour on the same day.

[P50]
The deputy captain’s gaze fixed on one of them.

[P51]
“Captain!”

[P52]

[P54]
“……!”

[P55]

[P56]
Why no word had come from the Qingcheng Sect—and where the brothers who had failed to return after seeing the emergency signal had gone.

[P57]

[P58]
“Everyone, attack! Kill hi—”

[P59]
Slash!

[P60]
The deputy captain’s shout was cut short.

[P61]

[P62]
*Can this truly be… the movement of a human being?*

[P63]

[P64]
He had failed to recognize the Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step performed by the greatest assassin under heaven—or rather, the greatest assassin in all history.

[P65]
Only death awaited him.

[P66]
Fwoosh!

[P67]
Blood erupted from the severed neck in a fountain. A figure brushed past the collapsing body and took another step, stirring a wind heavy with the scent of blood.

[P68]
Slash. Slash. Slash!

[P69]
The heads of the black-clad men who had watched their superior die in a daze flew into the air.

[P70]
Before the streams of blood could reach the ground, something pale and ghostlike swept through them.

[P71]
“It was the life I wanted so desperately.”

[P72]
Murmuring under his breath, he extended both hands. Long, slender threads streamed from his ten fingers.

[P73]
Beautiful and destructive threads of Sword Force.

[P74]
“And yet, why did you…”

[P75]
Whoosh!

[P76]
His ten curved fingers raked downward through the air, and Sword Force tore through space.

[P77]
Everything in its path was slashed apart. Shattered armor and weapons, severed limbs and heads—all flew in every direction.

[P78]
In a world brought to a standstill by blood and death, only one person moved freely.

[P79]
“…wake me?”

[P80]
Consumed by grief and fury, he was no longer the cheerful boy, nor was he the physician who had passed the name Divine Physician down to his Disciple.

[P81]
He had become the man he had been before earning the name Divine Physician. Before meeting the young carpenter who had fallen into despair after losing his wife and children to an epidemic. Before burying his weapons and leaving Murim behind.

[P82]
“The Slaughter Saint…!”

[P83]
Someone screamed the name.

[P84]
His eyes had sunk deeper than the abyss. He flung out both arms, and the wind—now a raging storm—swallowed more than a hundred black-clad men.

[P85]
Kwaaang!

[P86]
* * *

[P87]
A high hill stood east of the Sichuan Tang Clan.

[P88]
From there, one could see the entire Tang Clan estate at a glance. A small watchtower stood atop it, and martial artists had once taken turns standing guard.

[P89]
Once.

[P90]
Drip. Drip.

[P91]
Drops of blood fell from the watchtower and darkened the grass. Some rolled down the slope until they touched a hand.

[P92]
Its back was deeply wrinkled, and its nails had turned green from long years spent practicing poison arts.

[P93]
The hand belonged to Tang Sadok, the current Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan—the Myriad-Poison Asura.

[P94]
“Cough.”

[P95]
Blood sprayed from between his parched lips. His eyes, usually cold and forceful, looked ready to go out at any moment.

[P96]
“Is this how it ends?”

[P97]
Tang Sadok murmured faintly.

[P98]
Everything was racing toward its end. His life. The glorious history of the Sichuan Tang Clan.

[P99]
“Our family, built over centuries… brought down in a single day.”

[P100]
Tang Sadok’s lament rang hollow. He no longer possessed the strength even to feel anger or sorrow.

[P101]
His limbs crushed and his internal injuries severe, all the old Family Head could do was lean against an unknown tree and watch his clan perish.

[P102]
*This is my final gift to you.*

[P103]
The smiling face of a middle-aged man flashed before Tang Sadok’s eyes.

[P104]
The Western Heaven Demon Lord had not kept his promise. To him, the destruction of the Sichuan Tang Clan had been a foregone conclusion from the very beginning.

[P105]
“Urgh… Blergh!”

[P106]
The rage flaring within him like wildfire worsened his internal injuries. Tang Sadok vomited nearly half a gallon of blood, then gasped for breath.

[P107]
“I’m sorry. I’m sorry…”

[P108]
It was an apology to the ancestors of the Sichuan Tang Clan. To the innocent members of his household who had lost their lives because they had been saddled with an unworthy Family Head. And to Jin Taekyung and his companions, who had likely already met gruesome deaths at the hands of the Western Heaven Demon Lord.

[P109]
Of course, none of them could hear Tang Sadok’s voice.

[P110]
*If we meet in the afterlife, I will apologize to you myself.*

[P111]
Just as Tang Sadok murmured those words inwardly—

[P112]
Rustle.

[P113]
The bushes stirred, and he sensed something approaching.

[P114]
No. It was not human.

[P115]
Only when the strange presence had drawn right up to him did Tang Sadok realize who it belonged to.

[P116]
Hiss. Hiss.

[P117]
A flicking tongue. A horned, triangular head. A pure-white snake burrowed into Tang Sadok’s arms.

[P118]
“Ha… hahaha.”

[P119]
Tang Sadok slumped back with a laugh, both overjoyed and heartsick.

[P120]
“So it was you.”

[P121]
Hisss.

[P122]
The Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, Mimi, hissed as though answering her master. Her cold tongue licked his beard, which was matted with blood.

[P123]
“Clever creature. How did you find me all the way out here?”

[P124]
Tang Sadok gazed at his pet snake through clouded eyes.

[P125]
He had set her loose out of fear that she might be hurt in the chaotic battle. He had never expected them to meet again like this.

[P126]
Nor had he imagined their final farewell would happen this way.

[P127]
Rumble!

[P128]
A tremendous roar sent tremors all the way up the hill. The ground heaved, and the trees shook their branches.

[P129]
Tang Sadok raised his head and tried to find the source, but his failing eyesight could no longer make out what was happening.

[P130]
He could infer only one thing.

[P131]
*Has the time come?*

[P132]
It was a roar on an entirely different scale from Heaven-Shaking Thunder.

[P133]
At last, the destruction of the great Sichuan Tang Clan had reached his doorstep.

[P134]
Tang Sadok slowly closed his eyes, then opened them again.

[P135]
“Leave.”

[P136]
Hiss?

[P137]
The triangular head tilted to one side.

[P138]
“This old man has little time left. Neither does the Tang Clan. If you stay here, you will be caught up in this calamity as well.”

[P139]
Tang Sadok was the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan. Even if the Western Heaven Demon Lord did not come himself, someone would certainly come to confirm whether he was alive or dead.

[P140]
He could easily imagine what the murderers would do if they found the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake guarding her master’s side.

[P141]
“So go. Hurry!”

[P142]
He wanted to roar the words, but the voice he wrung out was so thin it seemed ready to snap.

[P143]
Yet the spiritual creature that had spent so many years beside him understood the final wish of the man who had been both her master and her friend.

[P144]
Drip. Drip.

[P145]
Warm droplets fell onto the back of Tang Sadok’s wrinkled hand.

[P146]
Leaving behind a few tears, Mimi slithered away, her white body gliding across the ground.

[P147]
As her presence receded into the distance, a bitter smile briefly touched Tang Sadok’s lips.

[P148]
“Yes. Go safely.”

[P149]
In his youth, he had roamed the battlefields. After the war, he had devoted his life to helping his father, the Poison King, rebuild the Sichuan Tang Clan.

[P150]
He had always been expected to remain cold and meticulous. He had no friend with whom he could share his heart, no lover, and no child of his own blood.

[P151]
Had that spiritual creature not remained by his side all those years, he could never have endured the loneliness.

[P152]
*From today onward, your name is Mimi. Tang Mimi.*

[P153]
On the day he first encountered the tiny Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, Tang Sadok had given her the Tang family name.

[P154]
They shared neither blood nor even species, but Tang Mimi was a member of the Sichuan Tang Clan, recognized as such by its Family Head.

[P155]
*I have lost everyone, and you alone are the one I send away alive. Hahaha.*

[P156]
Tang Sadok let out a hollow laugh and blinked.

[P157]
Through his fading senses, he heard distant roars and screams rising from below the hill.

[P158]
It must have been the final struggle of those fighting to stave off the clan’s destruction.

[P159]
*This old man is still here! I, Tang Sadok, Family Head of the great Sichuan Tang Clan, am here! Come to me!*

[P160]
The cry, as though wrenched from his throat with blood, never made it past the tip of his tongue.

[P161]
Tang Sadok felt the strength slowly drain from his entire body. His heavy eyelids sank lower, little by little.

[P162]
*I’m tired.*

[P163]
What if he simply closed his eyes and fell into a deep sleep?

[P164]
Perhaps, after a brief nap, he would awaken in the grand armchair in the Family Head’s Hall and find the familiar faces of his household waiting for him.

[P165]
How wonderful it would be if everything that had happened—including his father’s death—were nothing more than a Butterfly Dream.[^1]

[P166]
*Yes. If only it were.*

[P167]
His trembling eyelids slowly sank shut.

[P168]
No—they were just about to close.

[P169]
“Mimi! Quick Attack!”

[P170]
Hisssssss!

[P171]
“……?”

[P172]
*What the hell is this bullshit?*

[P173]
Tang Sadok’s eyes flew open.

[P174]
His vision suddenly cleared, revealing a young man racing toward him and Mimi’s white body shooting through the air like an arrow.

[P175]
“Y-You?”

[P176]
“Wow! A wild Grandpa Tang appeared!”

[P177]
Tang Sadok blinked at Cheongpung, who was grinning brightly despite the blood covering his face.

[P178]
“What… What is going on? How did you…?”

[P179]
Cheongpung answered energetically.

[P180]
“Mimi! Whirlwind!”

[P181]
Whirrrrr!

[P182]
Had Tang Sadok possessed even a shred of strength, he would have cursed them both out.

[P183]
Cheongpung and Mimi realized their mistake too late and bowed their heads.

[P184]
“Ah, I’m sorry.”

[P185]
Hiss.

[P186]
“……”

[P187]
Tang Sadok forgot that he had been half dead only moments ago and stared blankly at the man and snake before him. At last, he managed to speak.

[P188]
“Our family… What happened to our family?”

[P189]
“They all died.”

[P190]
“……!”

[P191]
“Oh. Not the Tang Clan. I meant Dark Heaven’s black-clad men.”

[P192]
*You should have said that first!*

[P193]
As Tang Sadok choked on shock and fury, Cheongpung pressed a finger to his Mingmen acupoint. Warmth like a spring day seeped into his body.

[P194]
“Cheongpung! True Qi Guidance!”

[P195]
*This bastard is going to keep this up until the very end…*

[P196]
Tang Sadok wanted to ask what had happened, but this time he could not resist the drowsiness washing over him.

[P197]
Just before his eyelids closed, a voice as gentle as a spring breeze reached his ears.

[P198]
“It’s all over now. Rest easy.”

[P199]
It was the voice that announced the end of a day longer and darker than any other.

[P200]
[^1]: The Butterfly Dream alludes to the ancient Chinese philosopher Zhuangzi’s dream that he was a butterfly, after which he wondered whether he was a man who had dreamed of being a butterfly or a butterfly dreaming of being a man.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.
